## Fatal

1. `fs-every-injective-module-is-projective` — Refutation step 1.1

The proof uses the Axiom of Choice without including it in the Statement or Given. It concludes that \(\mathbb Q/\mathbb Z\) is injective because it is divisible ([lines 35–47](/Users/ianx/Projects/prestige-math-library/items/fs-every-injective-module-is-projective.md:35)).

But the cited dependency explicitly states:

> “Assume the Axiom of Choice through Baer’s criterion… a module is injective if and only if it is divisible. … The converse inherits the Zorn-lemma use.”

See [thm-injective-modules-over-a-pid-are-exactly-divisible.md:31](/Users/ianx/Projects/prestige-math-library/items/thm-injective-modules-over-a-pid-are-exactly-divisible.md:31). Step 1.1 uses precisely the choice-dependent direction “divisible \(\Rightarrow\) injective.” The item’s Given names only \(I=\mathbb Q/\mathbb Z\), so the witness is not established under its stated assumptions.

Severity: **fatal — missing choice hypothesis / unlicensed inference**.

## Nonfatal

2. `ex-two-composition-series-of-the-cyclic-group-of-order-twelve` — Verification step 3.1

Step 3.1 says the adjacent quotient groups are cyclic “by [L1]” ([line 55](/Users/ianx/Projects/prestige-math-library/items/ex-two-composition-series-of-the-cyclic-group-of-order-twelve.md:55)). The cited dependency states only:

> “Every subgroup \(H\) of a cyclic group \(G\) is cyclic.”

See [thm-subgroups-of-cyclic-groups-are-cyclic.md:28](/Users/ianx/Projects/prestige-math-library/items/thm-subgroups-of-cyclic-groups-are-cyclic.md:28). It says nothing about quotients, so this changes the citation’s domain. The conclusion is nevertheless immediate because a quotient of a cyclic group is cyclic—or because step 2.1 already establishes prime quotient order.

Severity: **nonfatal — inaccurate citation, repairable within the 30-second threshold**.

No other fatal defect found.

Remaining published dependencies were sampled where their exact wording or provenance mattered. The provenance/dependency policy check passed for all 76 items; no assigned dependency targets an `ai-generated` Statement or Construction. Nothing was unavailable.
